backContent:
Meaning: Lasting for a very short time; transitory.

Synonyms:
• Temporary
• Fleeting
• Transient

Example: 'Fashion trends are often ephemeral, changing with every season.'

Meaning: Present, appearing, or found everywhere.

Synonyms:
• Omnipresent
• Pervasive
• Universal

Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.'

Meaning: Make something bad less severe, serious, or painful.

Synonyms:
• Alleviate
• Reduce
• Diminish
• Lessen

Example: 'Drainage systems were built to mitigate flood risks.'

Meaning: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically; practical.

Synonyms:
• Practical
• Realistic
• Sensible

Example: 'We need a pragmatic approach rather than an idealistic one.'

Meaning: Examine or inspect closely and thoroughly.

Synonyms:
• Inspect
• Examine
• Analyze

Example: 'Customers should scrutinize the terms and conditions before signing.'

Meaning: Seeming reasonable or probable.

Synonyms:
• Believable
• Credible
• Feasible

Example: 'She could find no plausible explanation for its disappearance.'

Meaning: Unwilling and hesitant; disinclined.

Synonyms:
• Unwilling
• Hesitant
• Loath

Example: 'He was reluctant to commit to any long-term plans.'

Meaning: Of considerable importance, size, or worth.

Synonyms:
• Significant
• Considerable
• Sizable

Example: 'The company made a substantial investment in AI research.'

Meaning: Make up for something unwelcome or unpleasant.

Synonyms:
• Make up for
• Offset
• Balance out

Example: 'Nothing can compensate for the loss of a loved one.'

Meaning: Cancel an event or agreement.

Synonyms:
• Cancel
• Abandon

Example: 'The match was called off due to heavy rain.'

Meaning: Postpone something until a later date; delay.

Synonyms:
• Postpone
• Delay
• Defer

Example: 'Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.'

Meaning: Think that someone is inferior or of low social status.

Antonym:
• Look up to (hayran olmak, saygı duymak)

Example: 'She looks down on people who haven't been to university.'

Meaning: Produce an idea, plan, or answer.

Synonyms:
• Devise
• Invent
• Propose

Example: 'Our engineering team came up with an ingenious solution.'

Kural: Subject + BE + V3 (Past Participle)

• Present: is/are + V3 ('The car is washed.')
• Past: was/were + V3 ('The letter was sent.')
• Modal: must be + V3 ('Rules must be obeyed.')

Meaning: Become progressively worse.
Synonyms: Worsen, decline, degenerate.
Example: 'His health began to deteriorate rapidly.'

Meaning: Open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning.
Synonyms: Vague, unclear, equivocal.
Example: 'The government gave an ambiguous statement.'

Meaning: Producing a great deal of profit.
Synonyms: Profitable, rewarding, money-making.
Example: 'Real estate can be a lucrative investment.'

Meaning: Continue in a course of action even in the face of difficulty with little prospect of success.
Synonyms: Persist, carry on, endure.
Example: 'Despite the setbacks, she persevered with her research.'

Meaning: Suddenly and unexpectedly.
Synonyms: Suddenly, without warning, hastily.
Example: 'The interview ended abruptly when he walked out.'

Meaning: Satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity.
Synonyms: Sufficient, satisfactory, enough.
Example: 'Make sure you have an adequate supply of water.'

Meaning: Complete; including all or nearly all elements of something.
Synonyms: Thorough, exhaustive, complete.
Example: 'This book offers a comprehensive guide to history.'

Meaning: Absolutely necessary.
Synonyms: Essential, vital, crucial.
Example: 'A smartphone is indispensable for modern work.'

Meaning: Deal effectively with something difficult.
Synonyms: Deal with, handle, manage.
Example: 'She struggled to cope with the heavy workload.'

Meaning: Resemble a parent or ancestor in appearance or character.
Synonyms: Resemble, look like.
Example: 'He takes after his father in temperament.'

Meaning: Cause something to happen.
Synonyms: Cause, lead to, produce.
Example: 'The new regulations brought about major changes.'

Meaning: Cease making an effort; surrender.
Synonyms: Abandon, quit, surrender.
Example: 'Never give up on your dreams.'

Meaning: Trust or have faith in someone/something.
Synonyms: Trust, count on.
Example: 'You can always rely on him in times of crisis.'
